Constraint: Committed scope must be baselined and controlled. Minimum business capabilities in the Master Project Brief section 3 must be delivered. Uncontrolled scope creep is not acceptable.
Engineering implication: Every requirement must trace to a stakeholder source. Additional features enter only through a change request with impact analysis. Six items were deliberately deferred rather than absorbed.

Constraint: Four assessed milestones inside a single SEN381 delivery period. Three part-time student engineers with concurrent modules.
Engineering implication: M1 must be baselined before consequential architecture work begins, otherwise M2 inherits an unstable foundation. Work is split into three parallel workstreams with a fixed integration point rather than sequential handover.

Constraint: Free or low-cost services only. Free-tier limits and likely operational cost beyond the educational context must be identified.
Engineering implication: Rules out paid messaging gateways (CF-03), managed object storage at scale (SCOPE-D-01) and always-on compute. Directly shapes the achievable performance and availability targets and therefore the M2 architecture.

Constraint: Quality attributes must be defined now and supported by measurable evidence later. Unsupported claims are not accepted.
Engineering implication: Every NFR carries a metric and a named verification method, even where the measurement itself only becomes possible in M3. NFRs without a measurement route were rewritten or removed.

Constraint: Security is a lifecycle responsibility from requirements onwards, not a final hardening pass.
Engineering implication: Authentication, authorisation, secrets handling, audit and privacy requirements are baselined in M1 so that M2 architecture cannot quietly design them out. Residual risk is recorded rather than a claim that the system is secure.

Constraint: Three students of mixed and partly unknown proficiency. Learning-curve risk must be treated as an engineering constraint.
Engineering implication: Technology selection is deferred to M2 so it can be made against an honest capability audit and a small proof of concept rather than familiarity or preference.

Constraint: Belgium Campus cannot guarantee that any chosen language, framework, service or deployment platform is available or supported on the institutional desktop platform (Master Project Brief section 25).
Engineering implication: Availability and compatibility must be verified on the actual build environment before the stack is committed in M2. A stack that only runs on one member's personal machine is a single point of failure.

Constraint: Protected main, pull requests for substantive change, and a minimum of two approvals from members other than the author. Self-approval is not accepted.
Engineering implication: With a three-person team, two approvals means unanimous consent from the other two members. Any single absence blocks every merge, so a review turnaround rule and an escalation path are required from the start.
